annotation.title_clean: Public Consultation on Artificial Intelligence and Singapore's Intellectual Property Regime
annotation.title_en: Public Consultation on Artificial Intelligence and Singapore's Intellectual Property Regime
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Ministry of Law (MinLaw) and Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS)
annotation.summary_en: Singapore's MinLaw and IPOS consultation paper seeking views on AI and IP law. It covers copyright (AI training under the computational data analysis exception, output infringement and responsibility allocation, human creativity in AI-assisted works) and patents (AI-assisted inventorship, AI-generated prior art). No embodied AI content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Seeks views on clarity and scope of the computational data analysis exception for AI training, including lawful access and rights-owner safeguards.
Asks how responsibility for AI output infringement should be allocated among developers, deployers and end users.
Reaffirms human authorship requirement and asks how human contribution in AI-assisted works should be evidenced.
Maintains that only a natural person can be a named inventor and asks how to assess human contribution in AI-assisted inventions.
Considers how large-scale AI-generated technical disclosures affect prior art and patent examination.
